title: introduce-adaptive-shot-sensitivity-ci-gate-with-contrastive-replay
author: Aisha Bennett
release_notes: Adds a new CI gate that detects regressions sensitive to number-of-shot formatting and introduces a deterministic contrastive replay tool to repro and triage failures.
description:
Motivation: Some regressions only manifest when examples/shot counts change (0-shot vs 1-shot vs 4-shot). Existing cohort and drift gates catch overall quality shifts but miss conditional failures tied to prompting style. This PR adds an adaptive shot-sensitivity CI gate that tests a compact set of prompt-sets across multiple shot contexts and flags regressions that are differential by shot count.

What this does (high level):
- Adds a new CI hook (shot-sensitivity-gate) that runs a lightweight, prioritized matrix of prompt-sets x shot-counts during PR gating. The gate compares a rolling baseline snapshot and reports differential regressions where delta_by_shot exceeds calibrated thresholds.
- Introduces a contrastive-replay utility which stores the minimal repro payload (prompt, shot configuration, seed, model hash) to reproduce the failure deterministically in local or CI replay lanes. This aids debugging by producing counterfactual side-by-side outputs for the baseline and candidate commits.
- Adds an adaptive weighting scheme: small, high-priority prompt-sets are weighted more aggressively; low-signal sets use decaying failure penalties to reduce noise from sporadic flakiness. Weight decay parameters are configurable in the CI config file.
- Integrates with our existing eval reporting: failed shot-sensitive entries surface as a new failure type in the existing regression dashboard with per-shot deltas and replay links.

Why it's different: Instead of a broad end-to-end smoke rerun, this gate focuses on prompt-context sensitivity (number-of-examples) and provides deterministic replay artifacts for faster root-cause. It is intentionally lightweight and tuned for PR feedback loops rather than long-running post-merge sweeps.

Implementation notes (single-string body):
- New files added: hooks/shot_sensitivity_gate.py (implements sampling, matrix run, comparison logic), tools/replay/contrastive_replay.py (repro harness, deterministic runner), ci/configs/shot-gate.yml (gate configuration and weights), docs/gates/shot-sensitivity.md (user guide and tuning instructions), tests/test_shot_gate.py (unit + integration smoke tests), eval/fixtures/shot-priority-list.json (prioritized prompt-sets), dashboards/migrations/add_shot_delta_fields.sql (dashboard schema).
- Sampling strategy: top-N prioritized prompts pulled from the master priority list; each prompt is executed at 0-shot, 1-shot, and 4-shot by default. The gate computes per-prompt per-shot metric deltas (e.g. exact-match, semantic-similarity) and then aggregates with the configured weights.
- Thresholding: supports both fixed thresholds and a historical z-score mode against a rolling baseline. Default is z-score backed with a minimum absolute-delta floor to avoid tiny numerical noise.

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests added for the comparison engine and replay serialization.
- CI matrix includes: lint, unit, smoke-eval (small matrix run), and replay-integration (replays a stored failing case).
- First CI run surfaced a nondeterministic ordering bug in the priority sampler; fixed in second commit by adding stable sort on priority+id.

Operational considerations:
- The default gate is enabled on the preview CI lane (non-blocking) for two weeks to collect signal, then will be flipped to optional failure-on-high-confidence regressions.
- Replay artifacts are stored in the same S3 bucket as other eval artifacts; retention 30 days by default. Keys are small (prompt + shot config + seed), so storage cost is minimal.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: opt-in preview on all eval-harness PRs (reports only).
- Week 2: escalate to soft-fail for high-confidence regressions (requires one approver override to merge).
- Week 4: evaluate false-positive rate and adjust decay/weighting; promote to hard-fail if <1% FP on two consecutive weeks.

Related: Links to ENG-2981 (prompt-set hygiene) and ENG-2999 (eval-dashboard enhancements) in Linear.

Author (Aisha Bennett): Clarified: baselines are tracked per-model-variant; the gate aligns by model family and quantization tag and falls back to family-level baseline when variant samples are sparse.
